question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for remodeling collagen and softening ligaments during pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin is produced during pregnancy to soften ligaments and joints, preparing the pelvis for delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why does joint looseness during pregnancy make women more prone to muscle or joint injury?

options.A: It causes rapid and uncontrolled bone growth in limbs.
options.B: It reduces joint stability across the entire skeletal system.
options.C: It stops bones from absorbing necessary dietary calcium.
options.D: It decreases the overall strength of muscle fibers.

explanation: When ligaments become loose, joints lose their normal tight support. This makes them much more prone to strain and injury during everyday tasks. You've got this!

question: In which direction does a pregnant woman's center of gravity shift as her uterus grows?
explanation: The growing uterus and fetus pull the body's weight forward, forcing the mother to adjust her posture to avoid falling. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: How does the body naturally balance out the forward pull of a growing belly?

options.A: By leaning the upper torso and shoulders backward
options.B: By increasing the calcium density in the lower leg bones
options.C: By shortening the overall length of the spinal column
options.D: By bending the knees forward at all times

explanation: Leaning backward helps the mother keep her balance over her feet, though it places extra stress on the back muscles. Think of it as a natural balancing act!

question: What is the medical term for the exaggerated inward curve of the lower back seen in pregnancy?
explanation: Lordosis is just the natural inward curve of the lower back. During pregnancy, it becomes more pronounced (exaggerated) to help balance out the heavy bump.

question: A pregnant patient complains of severe lower back ache after standing for hours at her market stall. What is the main cause?

options.A: Inflammation of the bone marrow inside the vertebrae
options.B: Early degeneration of the spinal discs from calcium loss
options.C: Direct pressure of the fetal head on the lumbar nerves
options.D: Fatigue of the lower back muscles due to exaggerated spinal curves

explanation: The muscles along the lower spine have to work overtime to keep the body upright against the forward pull of pregnancy, leading to tiredness and aches.

question: Which specific pelvic joint is most directly affected by symphysis pubis dysfunction?
explanation: Symphysis pubis dysfunction causes pain right at the front pubic joint where the two pelvic bones meet. It's a common area of discomfort!

question: Which everyday activity is most likely to trigger sharp pain in a pregnant woman with relaxed pelvic joints?

options.A: Deep breathing exercises while sitting upright
options.C: Writing notes with a heavy pen
options.D: Stepping out of a car with one leg at a time

explanation: Movements that involve stepping out sideways or widening the legs unevenly—like getting out of a car—put extra strain on relaxed pelvic joints.

question: What is the classic description of the walking pattern often seen in late pregnancy?
explanation: Pregnant women naturally widen their stance and swing their hips slightly more to maintain balance over relaxed joints and a heavy abdomen. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: Why do pregnant women often develop swollen ankles and feet by the end of the day?

options.A: Arterial pressure in the legs drops to zero when sitting down.
options.B: Kidneys stop filtering water entirely during the third trimester.
options.C: The bones in the feet expand to make room for extra weight.
options.D: The growing uterus slows down blood return from the lower legs.

explanation: Pressure from the heavy uterus on the large blood vessels in the abdomen slows down blood flow coming back up from the legs, causing fluid to pool in the feet.

question: What happens to the pelvic joints to help the baby pass through the birth canal during labor?

options.A: They yield and allow slight widening of the pelvic ring.
options.B: They lock firmly in place to protect the spinal cord.
options.C: They shrink in size to push the baby downward.
options.D: They temporarily fuse into a single solid bone.

explanation: Relaxed pelvic ligaments let the bones shift slightly, creating a bit more space for the baby to move safely through the pelvis.

question: A nurse is positioning a woman on the delivery bed for a long second stage of labor. What action helps protect her joints?

options.A: Elevating the head of the bed to a complete vertical sitting position
options.B: Ensuring proper joint alignment and adding supportive padding
options.C: Tying the legs tightly together to prevent excessive spreading
options.D: Massaging the calf muscles vigorously every five minutes

explanation: Proper body alignment and extra padding prevent unnatural twisting on relaxed ligaments during long periods in awkward positions.

question: What is the term for the separation of the front abdominal wall muscles that often happens during pregnancy?
explanation: Diastasis recti is simply the parting of the large front abdominal muscles to make room for the growing uterus. A very common finding in midwifery!

question: Why are new mothers still at risk for joint injuries in the weeks right after giving birth?

options.A: The sudden loss of body weight makes the skeleton extremely brittle.
options.B: New mothers stop using their muscles entirely while resting.
options.C: Relaxin hormone remains in the body for some time, keeping joints lax.
options.D: Breastfeeding draws all the calcium out of the arm and leg bones.

explanation: Even though delivery is done, relaxin takes several weeks to completely clear out of the bloodstream, leaving ligaments loose and vulnerable.

question: How does sleeping on the side with a pillow between the knees help a pregnant woman with back pain?

options.A: It prevents fluid from pooling in the upper body and arms.
options.B: It keeps the pelvis aligned and reduces twisting stress on the lower back.
options.C: It increases the amount of calcium absorbed by the spinal bones.
options.D: It completely stops the baby from moving around during the night.

explanation: Placing a pillow between the knees prevents the top leg from pulling the spine into an awkward twist while resting. Simple and effective advice for patients!

question: A nurse is teaching an antenatal class about preventing back strain. Which advice is best to share?

options.A: Lie flat on your back for long periods during the day to rest your spine.
options.B: Bend at your knees and keep loads close to your body when lifting objects.
options.C: Wear high-heeled shoes daily to strengthen your calf and ankle muscles.
options.D: Avoid all forms of physical activity until after the baby is born.

explanation: Good body mechanics—like lifting with the legs instead of the back—protect the vulnerable spine from unnecessary strain. Great teaching point!
